newsitem.title: GERMANY: Postbank signs cooperation deal with post office.
newsitem.headline: Postbank signs cooperation deal with post office.

text.p: Postbank AG, the banking arm of the Germany's Post AG mail service, said it had reached agreement with Post AG on co-operation over the use of post office counter space to distribute its services.
After a supervisory board meeting late on Wednesday, Postbank said it had immediately signed a cooperation deal drafted by German post and telecommunications minister Wolfgang Boetsch.
No details were given of the document's contents.

Boetsch welcomed the agreement, saying it showed a definitive will on the part of bank to work together with the postal authorities and opened the way for the Postbank's privatisation, expected sometime in 1997.
"With this (agreement), the foundation has been laid for the flotation of Postbank," the minister said.
In February, the German government said it would allow the post office to take a stake of up to 17.5 percent in Postbank, clearing the way for the privatisation of the bank later this year.
Postbank told Reuters on Monday that no date had yet been set for the bank's floatation, and that this could only be set after a co-operation agreement had been signed.
